message.reasoning_content:
Let me analyze the certificate markdown.

Certificate:
- Number: R117/2007-NL1-17.04 revision 1 → number "R117/2007-NL1-17.04", revision 1
- Project number: 1901827
- Page total: 3
- Member state: The Netherlands
- Date issued: 20 December 2017
- OIML issuer id: NL1

Issuing authority:
- Name: NMi Certin B.V., OIML Issuing Authority NL1
- Address: Hugo de Grootplein 1, 3314 EG Dordrecht, the Netherlands
- Person responsible: C. Oosterman
- Person title: Head Certification Board
- Phone: +31 78 6332332
- Email: certin@nmi.nl
- Website: www.nmi.nl
- oiml_issuer_id: NL1

Applicants: Endress + Hauser Flowtec AG, Kägenstrasse 7, CH-4153 Reinach, Switzerland

Manufacturers: same (Applicant and Manufacturer)

Certified type:
- Category: "Measuring system"? Actually it's a "measurement transducer" — per the category list, "Measuring transducer". The schema says category e.g. "Load cell", "Indicator", "Measuring system", "Fuel dispenser", "Taximeter", "Gas meter". Here it's a measurement transducer for dynamic measuring systems for liquids. I'll use "Measurement transducer" (as in the document: "A measurement transducer").
- Type designations: Promass Q 300 DNxxx, Promass Q 500 DNxxx — with footnote 1 (xxx denoting size of Promass Q measurement sensor). Type designations: "Promass Q 300", "Promass Q 500". The DNxxx is the sensor size. Actually types: "Promass Q 300 DNxxx[1]; Promass Q 500 DNxxx[1]". So type_designations: ["Promass Q 300 DNxxx", "Promass Q 500 DNxxx"] with footnote. Hmm. Or models: Promass Q 300, Promass Q 500.
- Module designation: The measurement transducer consists of measurement sensor + electronics. Not exactly "Analog load cell". Could be null. The cert covers "Promass Q 300" (DNxxx sensor + Promass 300 electronics) and "Promass Q 500" (sensor + Promass 500 electronics).

Model family: two models: Promass Q 300, Promass Q 500. Also sensor sizes DN25, DN50, DN80, DN100 — but the sensor is the same? Actually the measurement sensor sizes vary: DN25, DN50, DN80, DN100 with different max/min flow rates. The model matrix could be per sensor size. Hmm.

The Table 1 is "General characteristics of the Promass Q measurement sensor" with columns DN25, DN50, DN80, DN100 and rows: Max flow rate [t/h] 20/80/200/400; Min flow rate 0.45/2/6/14; Min Measured Quantity [kg] 10/20/100/200.

This is a matrix table: model_level entries per sensor size. So models could be DN25, DN50, DN80, DN100 for the sensor. But the whole instrument models are Promass Q 300 and Promass Q 500 (with electronics differing).

Approach: model_family.family_name = "Promass Q", models: [{"model_id": "Promass Q 300"}, {"model_id": "Promass Q 500"}]. Then matrix_tables for Table 1 (sensor characteristics by size). And model_level characteristics for sensor sizes: maximum_flow_rate, minimum_flow_rate, minimum_measured_quantity per sensor size (DN25, DN50, DN80, DN100).

Also, characteristics differ per electronics model (Promass 300 vs 500): environment classes (M3/E2 vs M3/E2/H3) and software versions. Could be model_level with models "Promass 300" and "Promass 500". Hmm, but models of the whole instrument are Promass Q 300 and Promass Q 500. The electronics are components: Promass 300 electronics, Promass 500 electronics, Promass Q measurement sensor.

Components:
- role: measurement sensor, type_designations: ["Promass Q measurement sensor"], characteristics per size.
- role: transmitter/electronics, type_designations: ["Promass 300", "Promass 500"], alternatives? Not alternatives — the two models. Actually "The Promass 300 and Promass 500 flow transmitter is solely to be used in combination of dynamic mass meters (Coriolis meters) of brand Endress + Hauser."

Let me structure:

components[]:
- {role: "measurement sensor", type_designations: ["Promass Q measurement sensor"], characteristics: {...}} — schema says components have role, type_designations[], alternatives, characteristics{}. The characteristics within components — I'll put sensor-level stuff into model_level characteristics of main characteristics instead, or into components' characteristics as type_level objects. The schema for components says characteristics{} — free-form. I could put the sensor table in matrix_tables and reference.

Simplify:

model_family:
  family_name: "Promass Q"
  models: 
    - {model_id: "Promass Q 300", attributes: {electronics: "Promass 300"}}
    - {model_id: "Promass Q 500", attributes: {electronics: "Promass 500"}}

But also sensor sizes. Perhaps models should include sensor size variants: Promass Q 300 DN25, etc.? The type designations include DNxxx with footnote saying xxx denotes sensor size. The sensor sizes are DN25, DN50, DN80, DN100 (from Table 1). So full model variants: Promass Q 300 DN25, Promass Q 300 DN50, ... 8 combos? That may be overreach. The certificate lists type: Promass Q 300 DNxxx; Promass Q 500 DNxxx. The table gives sensor characteristics per size, applying to both models.

I think a reasonable approach: models per sensor size for model_level flow characteristics (DN25, DN50, DN80, DN100), and model_level for electronics characteristics per Promass 300/500. But mixing model axes is confusing. Alternatively use matrix_tables for Table 1, and model_level entries keyed by sensor size for flow rates, plus config/model-level for electronics.

Given the schema, I'll do:

model_family: {family_name: "Promass Q", models: [{model_id: "Promass Q 300"}, {model_id: "Promass Q 500"}]}

characteristics:
  type_level:
    maximum_pressure: {value: 100, unit_symbol: "bar"}
    density_range: {value: {min: 400, max: 1400}, unit_symbol: "kg/m³"}
    maximum_viscosity: {value: 440, unit_symbol: "mPa·s"}
    ambient_temperature_range: {value: {min: -40, max: 55}, unit_symbol: "°C"}
    accuracy_classes: {value: "0.3; 0.5; 1.0; 1.5"}? Hmm — accuracy class is in recommendation.accuracy_classes. Maybe include environment class M3/E2/H3? That's per model (sensor H3, 300 electronics M3/E2, 500 electronics M3/E2/H3).
    product_temperature_range: two values: -10…+90 °C for mass, density and volume measurement; -200…+90 °C for mass measurement. This is config-level: attribute product_temperature_range, axis "measurement mode". Values: [{condition: "mass, density and volume measurement", value: {min: -10, max: 90}}, {condition: "mass measurement", value: {min: -200, max: 90}}].

  model_level:
    - attribute: maximum_flow_rate, unit_symbol: "t/h", values: [{model: "DN25", value: 20}, {model: "DN50", value: 80}, {model: "DN80", value: 200}, {model: "DN100", value: 400}]
    - attribute: minimum_flow_rate, unit_symbol: "t/h", values: [{model: "DN25", value: 0.45}, {model: "DN50", value: 2}, {model: "DN80", value: 6}, {model: "DN100", value: 14}]
    - attribute: minimum_measured_quantity, unit_symbol: "kg", values: [{model: "DN25", value: 10}, {model: "DN50", value: 20}, {model: "DN80", value: 100}, {model: "DN100", value: 200}]

Hmm, but the models are Promass Q 300 and Promass Q 500 — using DN sizes as model ids in model_level might conflict. Alternatively define models as the 4 sensor sizes? The certificate type is the measurement transducer (sensor + transmitter). The Table 1 covers the sensor by size.

Option: model_family models: Promass Q 300 and Promass Q 500, and the sensor sizes as config axis "sensor_size" in config_level:

config_level:
  - attribute: maximum_flow_rate, axis: "sensor_size", values: [{condition: "DN25", value: 20, unit_symbol: "t/h"}, ...]

That might be cleaner. But the R60 example uses model_level for variants. Both defensible. I'll use model_level with models named by DN size since Table 1 columns are the model variants for the sensor, and separately note electronics differences as model_level with model "Promass 300"/"Promass 500"? Mixing two axes in one model_level list is messy.

Alternative: put everything in matrix_tables (Table 1, Table 2, Table 3) and populate model_family with the instrument models and config_level for sensor size axis.

Let me decide: 

matrix_tables:
1. name: "General characteristics of the Promass Q measurement sensor", columns: ["sensor_size", "maximum_flow_rate", "minimum_flow_rate", "minimum_measured_quantity"], column_units: [null, "t/h", "t/h", "kg"], rows: 4 rows (DN25..DN100), then the shared characteristics (max pressure etc.) are type-level.
   Also rows for maximum pressure, density range, etc. with colspan=4 — those are same across sizes. I could include them as columns with same value each row, or leave them as type_level. I'll include the varying ones in rows and also keep full table? Simpler: matrix table with 4 size rows and the three flow columns; shared ones as type_level characteristics.

Actually to "preserve multi-dim tables", maybe include all columns. But repeated values add noise. I'll include just the per-size columns in the matrix table and put shared ones in type_level. Hmm, the table also includes accuracy class and environment class rows (colspan). I'll include environment class? The sensor env class is M3/E2/H3. I could add columns... no, keep it simple: columns sensor_size, maximum_flow_rate, minimum_flow_rate, minimum_measured_quantity.

2. Table 2: Promass 300 electronics: rows for environmental classes, ambient temp, power supply, software identification (3 versions). This is per-component. I could represent as matrix_tables with name "General characteristics of the Promass 300 electronics". Or as components entries with characteristics.

Components approach:
components:
- role: "measurement sensor", type_designations: ["Promass Q (DN25, DN50, DN80, DN100)"]... hmm type designations should be identifiers: "Promass Q measurement sensor". characteristics: {sensor_size: ...}? 

I'll do components:
- {role: "transmitter (electronics)", type_designations: ["Promass 300", "Promass 500"], alternatives: null, characteristics: {environment_classes: ..., ambient_temperature_range: ..., power_supply_voltage: ..., software_identification: ...}} — but the two electronics differ (H3, software versions). Could split into two components entries:
  - {role: "transmitter (electronics), Promass Q 300", type_designations: ["Promass 300"], characteristics: {environment_classes: "M3/E2", ambient_temperature_range: {min:-40,max:55} °C, power_supply_voltage: "24 VDC; 100…240 VAC; 50…60 Hz", software_versions: [...3 versions...]}}
  - {role: "transmitter (electronics), Promass Q 500", type_designations: ["Promass 500"], characteristics: {environment_classes: "M3/E2/H3", ..., software_versions: [...2 versions...]}}

The schema says components[].characteristics{} — free form, so structured values there. The strict structured-value rule says "Every characteristic value MUST be an object with this shape". I'll apply that to components characteristics too where sensible.

Power supply: "24 VDC; 100…240 VAC; 50…60 Hz". Split: power_supply_voltage_dc: 24 V; power_supply_voltage_ac: {min:100, max:240} V; power_supply_frequency: {min:50, max:60} Hz. I'll record as separate characteristics.

Software identification: multiple versions with CRCs. Record as a string list or as characteristic with value string. E.g. software_identification: {value: ["01.00.02 (CRC 0xE87F Modbus; 0x321F Hart)", ...]}. The strict shape says value is number|{min,max}|string. A list isn't allowed. So either multiple entries or one concatenated string. I'll use a string with semicolons, or separate characteristic entries software_version_1 etc. Hmm. I'll do "software_identification": {"value": "Version 01.00.02 (CRC 0xE87F Modbus, 0x321F Hart); Version 01.01.01 (CRC 0xA476 Modbus, 0x977D Hart); Version 01.01.02 (CRC 0x2AAB Modbus, 0xED44 Hart)"}. That's acceptable.

Actually maybe better to put software versions in a dedicated list per component. The schema's characteristics{} in components is free-form {} — the strict rule mentions "characteristic value" generally. I'll keep structured but allow strings.

Sensor component:
- {role: "measurement sensor", type_designations: ["Promass Q measurement sensor (DN25, DN50, DN80, DN100)"], characteristics: {maximum_pressure: 100 bar, density_range: 400-1400 kg/m³, maximum_viscosity: 440 mPa·s, environment_class: "M3/E2/H3", product_temperature_range...}}

Hmm, product temperature ranges are for the transducer overall presumably.

Let me now assemble the final JSON.

certificate:
- number: "R117/2007-NL1-17.04" (include "revision 1"? The revision_history covers it; number field: "R117/2007-NL1-17.04"). 
- scheme: "A" (single issuing authority, cert of conformity under OIML scheme A typically for these NMi certs). NMi as OIML Issuing Authority NL1 — these are scheme A certificates. Yes, OIML CSA is scheme A... Actually the OIML Certificate System for measuring instruments: Scheme A is "OIML-type evaluation and certification without scrutiny" — certificates issued by Issuing Authorities like NMi NL1. I'll set scheme: "A".

- category: "Measurement transducer"
- type_designations: ["Promass Q 300 DNxxx", "Promass Q 500 DNxxx"] — with footnote 1. Should I include footnote marker? type_designations is a list of strings; footnote markers can't attach. I'll list ["Promass Q 300", "Promass Q 500"] and mention DNxxx in description? The document literally: "Type: Promass Q 300 DNxxx[1]; Promass Q 500 DNxxx[1]". I'll use ["Promass Q 300 DNxxx", "Promass Q 500 DNxxx"] and footnotes[1] explains xxx = sensor size. Good.
- module_designation: null? The transducer... For R117, modules: measurement transducer. Not applicable. I'll set "Not applicable"? Rule: module_designation "Analog load cell" | "Not applicable" | null. For load cells it's used; here I'll use null or omit. I'll omit... Actually schema lists it; omit if not present. I'll omit.
- description: "Measurement transducer (Coriolis flow transmitter) comprising the Promass Q measurement sensor and Promass 300 or Promass 500 electronics; to be used solely in combination with dynamic mass meters (Coriolis meters) of brand Endress + Hauser." Something like that. Free-text if present — the doc describes. I'll craft a concise description.

model_family:
- family_name: "Promass Q"
- models: [{model_id: "Promass Q 300", attributes: {electronics: "Promass 300"}}, {model_id: "Promass Q 500", attributes: {electronics: "Promass 500"}}]

Should I add sensor size variants? The sensor sizes DN25-DN100 apply to both models. I'll add config_level axis "sensor_size" for the flow characteristics, OR model_level keyed by sensor size. The R137 example keyed models by size (G1.6). Here I think using config_level axis "sensor_size" is cleanest since the models are the two transmitters, and sizes are a configuration dimension of the sensor. Hmm, but is it a "configuration"? The type designation includes DNxxx, so it's part of the model naming. 

Given ambiguity, I'll include both: matrix_tables with Table 1, and model_level entries with model ids "Promass Q 300 DN25", ... no that's 8 combos but values are same for both electronics.

Simplest faithful representation: model_level entries with model = sensor size (DN25, DN50, DN80, DN100). The R60 example uses Emax values as model ids. Similarly here. I'll do that, and models in model_family as the two transmitters. Also add a note? No notes field.

Actually, let me reconsider: the flow rates are sensor characteristics; the sensor sizes are effectively sub-models. I'll put them in model_level with model ids "DN25" etc. Fine.

type_level:

- maximum_viscosity: {value: 440, unit_symbol: "mPa·s"}

- minimum_flow_rate (t/h): DN25 0.45, DN50 2, DN80 6, DN100 14

Should I include the shared rows in the table too? For fidelity, maybe include them as columns repeated. I'll keep them out and in description/type_level. Hmm, but rule 4 says preserve multi-dim tables. The colspan rows are effectively type-level. I think it's fine.

Also Table 2 and Table 3 as matrix_tables? They're single-column characteristics, not matrices. I'll represent them via components. But then Table 2/3 info lives in components[].characteristics. Good.

1. {role: "measurement sensor", type_designations: ["Promass Q measurement sensor"], alternatives: null, characteristics: {sensor_size: {value: "DN25, DN50, DN80, DN100"}, environment_class: {value: "M3/E2/H3"}, ...}} Hmm. Wait — is the environment class of the sensor M3/E2/H3? Table 1 "Environment class M3 / E2 / H3" — yes for sensor.
